item1_coercion.fix: _normalise_producer does an exact `in PRODUCERS` membership test; no strip()/lower() anywhere on the decision path (_claim_producer, derive_producer, _claim_standing)
item1_coercion.wrong_case_justification: assess.verdicts raises ProducerDeclarationError, but the docket layer must stay total for a rendering typo; capping is the same reject-don't-coerce rule (wrong case is rejected, never folded into model) and the reason is recorded on the claim's verdict_reason, so it is never silent
item1_coercion.strongest_remaining_attack: A hand-constructed MemberSpec can set verdict='CONFIRMS', verdict_producer='model' with no store row behind it and the cap grants CONFIRMS on that in-memory declaration. Not data-reachable: LaneSpec.from_store/from_json never populate the verdict fields (from_json does not even read candidate_id), and only materialize_lane attaches them, always from the store. Closing it means re-validating the verdict id against the store inside _claim_for.

item2_verdict_source.join_used: verdicts.claim_id = claims.id AND claims.candidate_id = candidates.id (SELECT v.id,v.claim_id,v.verdict,v.producer,c.candidate_id FROM verdicts v JOIN claims c ON c.id=v.claim_id WHERE c.candidate_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY v.id; highest verdicts.id per candidate wins)
item2_verdict_source.no_verdict_fallback: not CONFIRMS (fail-closed: declared CONFIRMS -> EXTENDS + reason naming the candidate producer)
item2_verdict_source.settled_by_note: there is no settled_by column in the store; decompose.ClaimSpec.settled_by is never persisted, so candidate->claims->verdicts is the only honest link

item3_vocabulary.fixture_decision: fixture is a per-row store class but collapses to unknown in BOTH _claim_producer and derive_producer, which is what removes the V5D divergence
